newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Carter Holt Harvey eases after strong run.
newsitem.headline: Carter Holt Harvey eases after strong run.

text.p: Shares in Carter Holt Harvey Ltd eased 1.7 percent on Tuesday in what brokers said was a correction to a sharp run-up over the last two months.
By 2.50 p.m. (0250 GMT) the forest products group was off six cents to NZ$3.47, following on from a three-cent fall on Monday.
But brokers said the stock had enjoyed a very strong run, particularly last week when it hit a high of NZ$3.60 -- a level not seen since October 1995.
"This brought some selling out, clearly, and they've come back a bit," John Rattray at Ord Minnett Securities said.
"You might rather ask what it was to put them up so much, but I guess that's a sentiment change towards pulp and paper," he said.
CHH started off April at just NZ$3.00, then began appreciating on the view that sentiment in the international pulp and paper sector may have finally turned the corner.
To a lesser extent, Fletcher Paper had experienced the same thing, peaking last week at NZ$3.42 and trading today at $3.36, down one cent on Monday's close.
